newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: ASIAN EXOTICS - Rupiah under siege as polls loom.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN EXOTICS - Rupiah under siege as polls loom.

text.p: * Indonesian rupiah continues slide on nervousness ahead of start of general election campaign.
* Malaysian ringgit weak but rangebound after overnight selling.
* Thai baht tracks dollar/majors, forwards come off on central bank chief's statement about lower interest rates.
* Singapore dollar stuck in range after early ringgit/Sing buying runs out of steam.
The beleaguered Indonesian rupiah headed lower on Friday as players remained nervous about possible unrest during the campaign for the May 29 general election, beginning on Sunday.
"People keep buying the dollar as they try to factor in possible riots or unrest during the campaign," a local bank dealer in Jakarta said.
Spot rupiah recovered slightly from a morning low of 2,440.5 and was quoted at 2,437.5/2,438.5 at 0440 GMT gainst an opening of 2,432.0/33.0.
"People are still bullish on the dollar," a U.S. bank dealer in Jakarta said, adding that the rupiah rebounded from lows on rumours of a possible band widening.
A U.S. bank dealer in Singapore said there were unconfirmed rumours Bank Indonesia had asked state banks to sell dollar/rupiah around the 2,440.0 level.
"But the market still seems to be caught short (dollars). There are still a lot of stop-loss buy orders on the upside," he said, adding that the dollar looked well supported around 2,433.0/35.0.
"We've seen some European and U.S. names offering dollars around 2,440.0 as well as the state banks. But I won't be surprised if we break that and go to test 2,445.0," he said.
He said the rupiah's weakness was being exacerbated by option-related and stop-loss dollar buying.
In Malaysia, the ringgit remained weak but was traded in a range after coming under pressure overnight.
Dealers said trading in dollar/ringgit had slowed down for lack of fresh leads and caution ahead of the weekend Group of Seven nations meeting.
"Nobody is buying (dollars) aggressively, but there is a negative sentiment in the market," a dealer with a Malaysian bank said.
He said rumours of a cabinet reshuffle had also hurt sentiment, while Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad's denial of the rumours had little impact.

The Singapore-based dealer said dollar/ringgit went to a high of 2.5070 in London overnight. "This morning KL banks were selling it back, thinking it's a little too high. But we're looking at a 2.5040-2.5080 range for the day," he said.

Further south, the Singapore dollar weakened early in the day on some ringgit/Sing buying by U.S. funds. But dealers said this was soon reversed, bringing the Sing dollar back from a low of 1.4453/55 to the U.S. dollar.
The local currency was expected to trade a 1.4435-1.4460 range to the U.S. dollar for the day.
In Thailand, the baht spot rate showed little reaction to the central bank governor's statement about the possibility of lower rates but dealers said baht forwards eased on the comment.
The baht was quoted at 26.081/26.084 to the dollar at 0440 GMT against 26.075/26.080 late on Thursday.
Bank of Thailand chief Rerngchai Marakanond said there was scope for currently high domestic interest rates to ease as interbank rates in the money market were now more stable.
"I had discussions with the Thai Bankers Association earlier. They said if the interbank rate can be kept below 10 percent for a month, there would be room for interest rates to come down," he said.
Overnight interbank rates have steadied to an average of around eight percent in April after rising sharply when the financial sector was in turmoil in March.
Dealers said the six-month rate had dropped from an opening off about 35 satangs to about 33/34 at midday.
"I think the spot is quite immune from all these negative comments at the moment. It's just basically tracking the G7 currencies," said a Singapore dealer.
-- Madhav Reddy in Kuala Lumpur (603-206 2323), Mantik Kusjanto in Jakarta (6221-384-6364), Anuchit Nguyen in Bangkok (662-652-0642) and Sonali Desai in Singapore (65-8703090)
